title: **Pelican Island Reservation, Volusia County ‡, Fla., established as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds** — the first federal bird reservation; boundaries described. † **Date:** the contemporary administrative record is unanimous for **March 14, 1903** — the USDA Solicitor's compilations of 1908 and 1913, the Biological Survey's FY1903 report, Palmer's Circular 87 (1912), and the Surveyor-General of Florida in the GLO report for FY1903, p. 317. **March 13** enters only through Roosevelt's own EO 1014 of 1909, which is where Lord's 1943 index appears to have taken it. Check the signed original before publishing either. ‡ **County: Lord is wrong.** The order names no county; its text runs "Pelican Island in Indian River in section nine, township thirty-one south, range thirty-nine east, State of Florida." The island lay in **Brevard County** in 1903 (St. Lucie was carved from southern Brevard in 1905, Indian River from northern St. Lucie in 1925). Volusia is fourteen townships north and nine ranges west.
